candidates.name: Awesome-Hospitality-Channel-Manager
candidates.what_it_holds: Curated link list (no data itself) of commercial channel-manager SaaS platforms (SiteMinder, Cloudbeds/myallocator, Cubilis, RateGain, D-EDGE, STAAH, eZee Centrix, HotelRunner, RoomCloud) and open-source integration code (QloApps, frappe/hospitality, ilgala/laravel-wubook, ChannexIO/php-sdk, vBridge/laravel-icalendar). Mentions industry market sizing (~$1.1-1.8B) with no citation. No datasets.
candidates.why_useful: Map of who the channel-manager vendors are and which have API SDKs, useful as a lead list if the team later wants to pull benchmark blog data from a vendor site (e.g. Cloudbeds/AirDNA market reports), but nothing pullable here itself.
candidates.time_coverage: n/a (link list, current as of repo)

candidates.name: Hostaway-PHP-SDK
candidates.what_it_holds: PHP SDK wrapping the Hostaway PMS REST API (listings, reservations, calendars, financials). No committed data; requires a paid Hostaway account + API credentials to pull anything.
candidates.why_useful: Would let a Hostaway-subscriber host or partner pull realised occupancy/ADR by property if the team ever gets access to a Hostaway account; not usable without credentials the team doesn't have.

candidates.name: guesty-client
candidates.what_it_holds: PHP wrapper for the Guesty API (property/reservation management). No committed data; requires a paid Guesty account. Last updated Feb 2019 (stale).
candidates.why_useful: Same pattern as Hostaway SDK — only useful with a live paid Guesty subscription the team does not have.

candidates.name: guesty-mcp-server
candidates.what_it_holds: 38 MCP tools exposing a connected Guesty account's reservations, listings, and financials to an AI agent. Requires the operator's own Guesty account credentials; no public data.
candidates.why_useful: Not usable for us without a Guesty account of our own; flagged only because it shows the shape of data Guesty exposes (occupancy, ADR, reservation pipeline) if we ever partnered with a manager willing to share access.

candidates.name: guesty-cli
candidates.what_it_holds: Independent Python CLI wrapping the Guesty PMS API with local sync of a connected account's listings/reservations to local files. No committed sample data; requires the operator's own Guesty credentials.
candidates.why_useful: Only relevant if the team can get read access to a real vacation-rental manager's Guesty account (e.g. through a contact) — would then give a clean local occupancy/ADR export mechanism.

candidates.name: air_dna_scraper
candidates.what_it_holds: Selenium scraper configured to pull AirDNA's general city-level STR metrics (occupancy, ADR proxies) currently set up for Washington State cities. No committed output data visible; scrapes a paid/login-gated AirDNA market-data page.
candidates.why_useful: AirDNA is the closest free-adjacent proxy for realised STR occupancy/ADR (gap #2), but this specific tool scrapes a page that sits behind AirDNA's paywall/ToS — a human ToS call, not runnable under our rules as-is.
candidates.size_hint: scraper code only, no committed data

candidates.name: rental-averages
candidates.what_it_holds: Application that processes AirDNA API output to compute mean occupancy and ADR. Requires a paid AirDNA API key; repo description gives no evidence of committed sample data, city list, or years covered.
candidates.why_useful: Shows the shape of an AirDNA-derived occupancy/ADR aggregator; not usable without an AirDNA subscription, and unverified whether any sample output is committed.

candidates.name: STR Analytics Python Client (exact repo path unverified — found via GitHub topic listing, not directly fetched)
candidates.what_it_holds: Described (via topic-page summary) as a Python client computing occupancy, ADR, and RevPAR with 12-month rolling calendars 'from Airbnb data' — likely a wrapper around scraped/derived Airbnb calendar data rather than a PMS product. Could not verify exact owner/URL or confirm committed data before hitting GitHub search rate limits (429, 1hr cooldown) mid-session.
candidates.why_useful: If it is what it claims — a generic occupancy/ADR/RevPAR calculator over calendar data — it could be reusable methodology on top of Inside Airbnb calendars we already hold (gap: turning raw calendars into occupancy/ADR/RevPAR consistently). Needs verification; flagged as unverified lead.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: possibly overlaps our own Inside Airbnb calendar/reviews processing

candidates.name: Short-Term Rentals Warehouse
candidates.what_it_holds: Described via GitHub topic page as a pipeline/warehouse/visualization project (Snowflake + dbt) investigating Airbnb's impact on housing; 15 stars. Could not confirm exact owner/URL or whether raw data is committed vs. only a dbt transformation pipeline over externally-supplied data before hitting rate limits.
candidates.why_useful: If it ships a runnable dbt pipeline against a public housing/STR data source, it could be a reusable ETL pattern for combining STR supply with housing data (gap #13 STR<->LTR crossover); needs a follow-up direct fetch to confirm the exact repo and its data source.

candidates.name: Shared Accommodations
candidates.what_it_holds: Python/pandas analysis of peer-to-peer rental effects on San Francisco's housing market, 10 stars. Exact owner/URL and whether source data is committed (vs. pointing to Inside Airbnb, which we already hold for other cities but not necessarily this exact SF cut) unverified before rate limiting hit.
candidates.why_useful: Possible SF-specific STR-vs-housing dataset/analysis; SF is not in our current 13-city Inside Airbnb panel, so if it commits its own SF data extract that would be a genuinely new city.
candidates.duplicate_of_holding: possibly derived from Inside Airbnb (which we hold for other cities, not confirmed for SF)

candidates.name: reviews-dashboard
candidates.what_it_holds: Full-stack dashboard aggregating reviews across Airbnb/Hostaway and Google for a property manager's own listings. Requires the operator's own API keys/business accounts; no public dataset.
candidates.why_useful: Not directly usable (needs a manager's own accounts), but demonstrates that Hostaway exposes normalized cross-platform review data, which is the kind of thing a cooperating STR manager could export if the team found one willing to share.

notes: This theme is genuinely thin on GitHub. Systematic search was badly hampered: (1) the WebSearch tool returned 'session web search budget exhausted (200/200)' for every query from the very first call, before this scout ran any — a shared session budget across concurrent scout subagents, not this scout's own usage; zero WebSearch queries actually ran. (2) Fell back to WebFetch against github.com/search and github.com/topics pages directly; github.com/search rate-limited to 429 (Retry-After 3600s) after ~6 queries and stayed blocked for the rest of the run; github.com/topics/* pages kept working throughout and were used for the remainder. (3) DuckDuckGo HTML endpoint served a CAPTCHA to the fetcher; Bing's SERP is JS-rendered and returned no usable snippets via WebFetch. Substantively: the PMS/channel-manager space (Guesty, Hostaway, Lodgify, OwnerRez, Hostfully, Smoobu, Beds24) is a B2B SaaS market where the public GitHub footprint is almost entirely (a) commercial API-client SDKs and MCP servers that require a paying customer's own account credentials to pull anything, useless to us without a cooperating host/manager, and (b) generic hotel/PMS software with no bundled data. AirDNA — the natural free-adjacent proxy for realised STR occupancy/ADR (gap #2) — has several scraper repos but scrapes a paywalled/ToS-gated site, so per our rules these are catalogued as unrun methods only, not data. No repo found here holds a committed, reusable occupancy/ADR/RevPAR dataset from any PMS or channel manager. Two unverified leads (a Snowflake/dbt 'Short-Term Rentals Warehouse' project and a San Francisco 'Shared Accommodations' housing analysis) surfaced only as topic-page summaries without exact owner/URL before the github.com/search rate limit hit; a follow-up scout with a working search budget should re-run `site:github.com "short-term rentals warehouse" dbt` and `site:github.com "shared accommodations" san francisco airbnb pandas` to pin these down, since dbt pipelines over housing data could plug gap #13 (STR<->LTR crossover). Recommend: if another scout has WebSearch budget remaining, hand this theme back to them; if `gh search` capacity opens up later (explicitly disallowed for this modality run), it would likely surface committed-data repos this web-only pass could not reach because of the rate limits encountered.
